intro: One world, three hosts. The seal above it is the hash of its canonical form.

steps.caption: Host A parses the world, canonicalizes it and seals it: sem-67e954cf….
Host B, a different machine, a different day: the same bytes, the same canonical form, the same seal.
steps.takeaway: Identity is computed, not assigned: every host derives the same seal from the same canonical form.

steps.caption: Host C, forever. The conformance suite asserts this fixture on every change.
Change one relation in the world. A different future needs a different seal, and it gets one: this is W′, not W.
steps.takeaway: Two artifacts with different futures have different seals; a preserved seal is a preserved meaning.

steps.caption: Nothing was named by a database row, a file path or a host. Location is not identity — that is the anti-pattern this answers.
steps.takeaway: Location Leak: encoding placement into identity when placement is not semantic.
